HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES

Chair Julie Lie called the meeting to order at 4:01 p.m.

  Commissioners Absent: Howat, Killion

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Joseph Botelho, Community
Program Specialist V, Jennifer Santana, Community Program Specialist.

  • Member Killion resigned May 29, 2026.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  • Chair Julie Lie provided and update, the subcommittee has not been able to
  meet since January due to quorum issues. The next scheduled meeting is
  June 8, 2026 at 2:00 p.m.
  Policy Subcommittee Meeting
  • Chair Sarah Bedy provided an update regarding the most recent
  subcommittee meeting. The subcommittee discussed the final policy
  recommendations and the Annual Report.
  • The subcommittee also reviewed the Mayor’s Fund pilot program project,
  which is agendized and will be discussed as a separate item later in the
  meeting.
  • Additionally, the subcommittee discussed a draft recommendation letter
  regarding the fencing surrounding the Billie Jean King Main Library. The
  subcommittee is seeking feedback from the Committee on the proposed
  recommendations.
  • Commissioners provided feedback and recommendations on the draft letter.
  The item will be agendized for the next meeting for final approval before
  being forwarded to the Mayor and City Council for consideration.
  CoC representative updates
  • City staff provided an update from the most recent General Membership
  meeting. During the meeting, PATH presented an overview of the services it
  will provide as the new operator of the City's four shelter sites.
  • The presentation included information on PATH's service model, program
  operations, and plans to support individuals experiencing homelessness
  through shelter, housing navigation, and supportive services. There was also
  discussion on the close out of the CDBG grant regarding PHK at 1725, the
  former best western.
  • Additional updates regarding the NOFO will be provided during agenda item
  #6.

3.  26-55278  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, consider appointing members of
  the Homeless Services Advisory Committee to serve on the Mayor's Fund
  Subcommittee.

  • The chair Julie Lie provided an overview of the Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  and encouraged members to join. At this time, no members expressed
  interest in joining the subcommittee.

4.  26-55275  Recommendation to review and approve the 2025 Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee Annual Report and policy recommendations.

  A motion was made by Member Hilliard, seconded by Member Wood, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Lie, Wood, Scott,  Russell,  Romero-Duran,  Noble,  Hilliard,
  Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Killion, Howat

  • Policy Subcommittee Chair Sarah Bedy presented the final policy
  recommendations to the Committee. Following discussion, the Committee
  determined that the recommendations are ready for approval.
  • Staff will update the recommendations with the 2026 Point-in-Time (PIT)
  Count data once it becomes available. Upon completion of those updates,
  the final recommendations will be forwarded to the Mayor and City Council
  for consideration.
  • The committee moved to approve the recommendation.

5.  26-55276  Recommendation to discuss a proposal for a $50,000 budget plan for the Mayor’s
  Fund pilot hygiene project to submit to the Mayor’s Fund.

  A motion was made by Member Wood, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Lie, Wood, Scott,  Russell,  Romero-Duran,  Noble,  Hilliard,
  Chotiswatdi, Bedy

  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None

  • The subcommittee chair Sarah Bedy provided an update on the discussion
  from the last subcommittee meeting. The subcommittee would like the
  Homeless Services Bureau staff to forward this letter to Mayor and City
  Council as a recommendation.
  • Commissioners engaged in conversation regarding this recommendation.
  They provided feedback regarding the proposal. Staff advised that this item
  would be agendized at the next HSAC meeting with final updates as
  a recommendation to the Mayor and City Council with funding provided
  through the Mayor’s Fund.
  • A member of the public provided feedback emphasizing the importance of
  maintaining hygiene services. He stated that discussions regarding security
  logistics should be addressed by the City Council and did not believe those
  details should be considered within this forum. The member further noted
  that the most important aspect of these programs is establishing clear
  metrics to measure success and evaluate outcomes.
  • Member Hilliard inquired whether the City plans to provide public restrooms
  in connection with the upcoming Olympic Games, noting that the event is
  expected to bring hundreds of tourists to the city and may increase demand
  for public restroom facilities.

6.  26-55277  Recommendation to discuss updates on the FY 2026 Continuum of Care (CoC)
  Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).

  A motion was made by Member Chotiswatdi, seconded by Member Wood, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Lie, Wood, Scott,  Russell,  Romero-Duran,  Noble,  Hilliard,
  Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Killion, Howat

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided and overview
  • HUD released the 2026 Continuum of Care (CoC) Notice of Funding
  Opportunity (NOFO) with approximately $4.04B nationally.
  • Key set-asides include:
  o $104M DV Bonus funding
  o $1.3B for new Transitional Housing (TH) and Supportive Services

  Page 4 of 8
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 3, 2026
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 4:00 PM

  Only (SSO) projects
  o $430M minimum for permanent housing serving families with children
• Long Beach CoC estimated:
  o $1.8M CoC Bonus
  o $1.9M DV Bonus
  o $12.16M total Annual Renewal Demand
  o About $7.3M in Tier 1 (protected funding) and $4.86M in Tier 2
  (competitive funding)
• Increased emphasis on Transitional Housing (TH), supportive Services
  participation requirements and employment/self-sufficiency outcomes
• Concern that more renewal projects nationwide (including locally) may lose
  funding.
• Projects are ranked using a structured scoring system, at least 50%
  objective criteria and 25% system performance measures.
• Scoring changes include sliding scale scoring instead of pass/fail thresholds
  and removal of low-value metrics that did not differentiate performance
• Reallocation means shifting funds based on performance or underspending.
• Can be voluntary (provider returns funds) or involuntary (poor performance
  or low expenditure)
• No limits on how much individual projects can request.
• Long Beach CoC is separate from LA City/County CoC system.
• HUD evaluates CoC-wide performance, not just individual projects.
• Funding is competitive nationally across CoCs.
• No single definition of “success” in homelessness programs.
• Potential loss of funding for renewal projects, especially in Tier 2.
• New eligibility/service requirements may exclude people with severe mental
  illness and chronically homeless individuals
• Risk of shifting toward more punitive or compliance-based models.
• Capacity issues, Limited housing placements, staffing constraints to meet
  new service expectations
• Concern that system changes may disadvantage some vulnerable
  populations.
• Board review and approval of: Scoring and ranking policies, Reallocation
  framework, Funding priorities
• Final HUD application due August 26, 2026 awards expected December 1,
  2026.
• The Committee engaged in discussion and asked clarifying questions
  regarding funding allocations, eligibility categories, reallocation processes,
  and HUD’s selection methodology.
• Public comment included suggestions to increase opportunities for new
  providers and innovative program models, as well as feedback emphasizing
  the need for continued focus on street-level conditions and reducing
  unsheltered homelessness.
• The Committee acknowledged the need to continue evaluating program

  design options in alignment with federal guidance while ensuring local
  priorities and population needs are addressed.

7.  26-55273  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Lie, Wood, Scott,  Russell,  Romero-Duran,  Noble,  Hilliard,
  Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Killion, Howat

  • Health Department staff Paul Duncan provided and update on the fiscal year
  2026/2027, at the moment the bureau is not filling any new positions or
  vacancies, reductions in overtime, and prioritizing services to reduce
  expenditures.
  • Measure A funding through the Los Angeles County Affordable Housing
  Solutions Agency (LACAHSA), this coming years funding for Renter
  protection and Homeless prevention stays relatively flat at $4.6M for the next
  fiscal year.
  • The city continues to advocate to the California State legislatures for
  increasing HHAP round 7 to the previous commitments of the $1B annually
  and to commit funding to a HHAP round 8.
  • Encampment Resolution Fund (ERF) round 5 Notice of Funding Availability
  (NOFA) is open and closes at 6/30.
  • The city has launched its Renter Aid program through LACAHSA Measure A
  Funding.
  • City staff and commissioners engage in conversation regarding the program,
  number of applicants and the number of applicants that they plan to award.
  • Commissioners ask staff about the strategic plan and whether the report will
  be brought to the commission for review. Staff will send out the
  Homelessness Strategic Plan Update – Community Engagement Report.
  • The Youth navigation center opened on the week of May 18th and has 12
  beds for Transitional Aged Youth (TAY) between ages of 18-24.
  • There are 480 households on vouchers at risk of losing rental assistance, on
  5/6 HUD released PIH Notice 2026-12 providing an overview of Federal
  Fiscal Year 2026 funding for the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program.
  • HSB provided response along the riverbeds for both the oil spill and
  chemical tank concerns in Garden Grove.
  • The HSB team is working to finalize the 2026 homeless count to be released

  later in June.

8.  26-55281  Recommendation to discuss and approve the meeting schedule for the
  Homeless Services Advisory Committee and subcommittees.

  A motion was made by Member Wood, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Lie, Wood, Scott,  Russell,  Romero-Duran,  Noble,  Hilliard,
  Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Killion, Howat

  • The Committee agreed to continue meeting on a bi-monthly basis, with
  meetings remaining scheduled from 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
  • Beginning in August, the permanent meeting location will be the Multi-
  Service Center.
  • In the event that the Multi-Service Center is unavailable during the winter
  months due to Inclement Weather Shelter activation, meetings will be
  relocated to the Housing Authority offices or the Billie Jean King Main
  Library, subject to availability.

9.  26-55274  Recommendation to approve future agenda items.

  A motion was made by Member Wood, seconded by Member Bedy, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Lie, Wood, Scott, Russell, Romero-Duran, Noble, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Killion, Howat, Hilliard

  • The Homeless Services Bureau staff will send out a list of future agenda
